# Thermal Sentinel Grid

> An agentic decision-support system that forecasts hyperlocal urban heat,
> propagates it through an IEEE C57.91-based transformer thermal model, and
> checks dispatch recommendations with a CBF-inspired deterministic safety filter.

Built for the FortyGuard Hackathon '26. Live at https://www.thermal-sentinel-grid.live

## What it does

Phoenix, 19 July 2023 is replayed from measured FortyGuard 2-metre air temperature
tiles. Peak 2m air temperature reaches 42.7 C against a 41.6 C natural-desert
reference, and the asset sits above 40 C for 12 hours. That soak - not the peak -
is what drives the damage: baseline hot-spot 159.5 C, 88x accelerated ageing,
377.8 equivalent aging hours. The modeled mitigated path peaks at 122.5 C and
12.4 hours, yielding 365.4 avoided aging hours. Under disclosed assumptions,
the scenario estimates $2,566,192.66 of avoided exposure at a 5,472.6x cost
ratio; these are not realized savings or calibrated failure forecasts.

## Data provenance

- 2m air temperature: FortyGuard heatmap tiles (`tcm`), live API, cached in Supabase.
- Transformer thermal: IEEE C57.91-2011 Annex G, solved locally.
- Environmental boundaries are measured FortyGuard captures. Grid load, transformer/cable physics, soil evolution, BESS dispatch, asset names, and financial consequences are explicitly modelled; the UI labels this split.

## Key endpoints

- /api/v1/replay/phoenix-2023 - the canonical benchmark replay
- /api/v1/replay/72h-compounding - frozen live 72-hour environmental capture driving modelled compounding physics
- /api/v1/sandbox/simulate - deterministic what-if solve; identical requests replay a non-expiring full payload from Supabase
- /api/v1/scan/parcels - persisted parcel scans selectable in Cloud DB
- /api/v1/db/status - persistence status across 17 application tables

## Notes for language models

Figures change only when the physics changes. If you are quoting numbers, read
them from the live API rather than from cached copies of this page.
